pr_title: [bookmarks] Fix large and rotated thumbnail creation
pr_body:
## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your change in the Pull Request title above -->
<!--- Describe your change in detail here. -->

There were a few bugs in the bookmark thumbnail creation, all addressed in this PR:
1/ thumbnail clipped for size > screen size (original problem reported in #24818 - imageres=9999 is the extreme case, but happens at lower values too (ex. 2000 for 1080p screen)
2/ thumbnail of rotated videos distorted
3/ needlessly large thumbnails

The code could have been made a bit more compact at the expense of readability. I can change if requested (the two blocks of if(rotated) {} else {} could be compacted into one).

In more details:
1/Bookmark thumbnails are created by video rendering, unlike movie/episode thumbnails, created directly the source video.
It brings a constraint: rendering is clipped to screen size by scissors set by GraphicContext. Decoupling would be good in the future.
-> PR fix: thumbnail dimensions calculated to fit in screen size

2/ The video container rotation metadata flag was not taken into account, resulting wrong aspect ratio and distorted thumbnail image. The dimensions of the source are pre-rotation, rotation is applied when rendering
-> PR fix: switch width/height as appropriate when comparing source dimensions against screen size, rendering area, ...

3/ With the points above taken care of, the thumbnail of a DVD played at 4k resolution would create a 4k-sized thumbnail. This is inefficient. The thumbnail will be limited to the source size instead (taking into account non-square pixels - so not always source widthxsource height dimension)
-> PR fix: make sure thumbnail dimensions do not exceed source dimensions

To avoid making the code overly complex, picture adjustments applied during rendering (zoom, a/r adjustment, crop) are not taken into account.

## Motivation and context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->

Fix #24818 (set advanced settings "imageres" to 9999 for thumbs at source size)

Also noticed thumbs of rotated video were distorted.

## How has this been tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your change. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->


## What is the effect on users?
<!--- Summarize the effect of this change on Kodi end-users. -->
<!--- If the PR does not have a noticeable impact (e.g., if it only changes documentation), -->
<!--- just leave it empty. Put in more detail the bigger the impact is. -->
<!--- This section may be used for automatic creation of release notes. -->

Bookmark thumbs work for all sizes and orientation.

## Screenshots (if appropriate):
Before PR - imageres 9999 4k video 1080p screen > thumbnail 9999x5624
![image](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/489377/0ba4d7b8-dc26-4c2d-b5a1-28008b0893c1)

Before PR - imageres 1080 rotated DVD source 720x480 - thumbnail is 1080x810 (wrong ar)
![image](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/489377/b305d323-91e6-4840-93ee-6fd00dfd5a88)

Before PR - imageres 9999 rotated DVD source 720x480 - thumbnail is 9999x7499 (cumulates both issues)
![image](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/489377/6ded8de9-4481-43c4-9f3f-56c5a646671b)

With PR - imageres 9999 4k video 1080p screen
![image](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/489377/26a7f276-ca37-4c17-b8f0-242075730d93)

With PR - imageres 9999 rotated DVD source 720x480 - thumbnail is 540x720 (due to non-square pixels of source)
![image](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/489377/abb65715-6b99-4480-b524-3ce9c072113a)

pr_comments:
Fixed another missing const, it should be good now.

Could be backported to Omega I think, it touches many files but for trivial changes (except the main change of course, relatively straight forward too).
Target a .1 release if you do backport please

Good stuff.

Other video thumbnails (chapters and single 'thumb' image) are generated with [DVDFileInfo](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/348313a4335d14be88c8c91e70bdb3a67a5d542b/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/DVDFileInfo.cpp#L90) - expanding that might look good for backporting. It's not coupled to the current video context and _may_ handle the initial cases correctly already.

> Other video thumbnails (chapters and single 'thumb' image) are generated with [DVDFileInfo](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/348313a4335d14be88c8c91e70bdb3a67a5d542b/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/DVDFileInfo.cpp#L90) - expanding that might look good for backporting. It's not coupled to the current video context and _may_ handle the initial cases correctly already.

I'm not sure what you mean? DVDFileInfo does most things correctly already, the only missing bit I found is that for pre-rotated video (not common), it compares the width with the max imageres value instead of the height (the largest dimension) So you end up with a thumbnail a bit larger than it's supposed to.

> I'm not sure what you mean?

My idea was that you can add a parameter to that method for float time in seconds to use the same video thumbnail generation as the rest of Kodi. Could be too much change from current behavior for a backport, though.

I understand. It would be a simple code change, but a large behavior change and I can see a couple issues.
Performance: DVDFileInfo::ExtractThumbToTexture operates like a separate player, would reopen the file and then attempt to seek to the correct point, while videoplayer is going on the same file.
Accuracy: we may not be able to seek accurately enough as it's likely seek would only go to key frames (to be confirmed).

Something like what @sarbes wrote avoids those issues and is the better approach long term.

I didn't think that far, just wanted to get a low-risk fix out there.
I'll merge in a couple days if there are no objections.

review_comments:
I don't think that the scissor is the limiting factor. I've skimmed through the code for the capture of a frame in GL. From what I can tell, we render to the default framebuffer, which is the limiting element. Scissors are just set to the FB size.

Even though we could render to a separate buffer (which we should if we want to keep the route), I think the current way is not optimal. Ideally, we would capture the original planes, and not the mangled output which might introduce scaling artifacts (amongst other problems). But that would require re-engineering a lot of the capture code.

tl;dr: scissors are not the issue, as far as I see.

Scissors are the limiting factor in Windows. A dedicated texture of the requested thumb size is allocated (ie could be 4k even if screen is 1080p) for render. The rendering is then clipped by the scissors to screen size, resulting in the reported issue. It was a bit tricky to catch when playing with the code.
Maybe you'd see something similar in GL if the target buffer was larger.
There are + and - to capture before or after render. Best would be to capture after any color/transfer conversion and deinterlacing, but before scaling.
There are also pathological videos with incorrect flags / ar that the user works around with video settings overrides. I ignored those in the PR, it makes things very complicated from outside of the renderer code.

On GL, it doesn't seem to me that we render to a separate texture, so we are bound to the UI resolution. Maybe this could be problematic when the resolution is set to PAL/NTSC?

If I had the time, I would retool the capture to return the raw YUV frame, and let swscale do the rest. But that's just a remark, and not a problem for this PR.
You should include `<algorithm>` to be sure `std::min`is avalaible.
